entries.title: You are approaching a zebra crossing and a pedestrian is waiting to cross. What should you do?

question.prompt: You are approaching a zebra crossing and a pedestrian is waiting to cross. What should you do?
options: Maintain your speed unless they step onto the crossing
Give way and be prepared to stop
Sound your horn to warn them
Wave them across while continuing to drive
question.explanation: You should give way to pedestrians waiting to cross at a zebra crossing. Never wave or signal them across because another vehicle may not have seen them.

entries.title: When may you use a motorway hard shoulder?

question.prompt: When may you use a motorway hard shoulder?
options: To make a phone call
To overtake slow traffic
In an emergency or when directed by an authorised signal or person
Whenever traffic is congested
question.explanation: You must not use a hard shoulder except in an emergency or when directed by the police, traffic officers or a traffic sign. Some motorways have a hard shoulder that can be opened as a running lane when signs permit.

entries.title: What is the main purpose of a correctly adjusted head restraint?

question.prompt: What is the main purpose of a correctly adjusted head restraint?
options: To make the seat more comfortable
To reduce the risk of neck injury in a collision
To support luggage on the back seat
To improve rear visibility
question.explanation: A correctly adjusted head restraint helps reduce the risk of neck injury, particularly whiplash, in a collision.

reviewImage.label: Head restraint adjustment
reviewImage.visualDescription: Head restraint beside the back of a seated person's head

entries.title: On a high-speed road in wet weather, how should you change the normal two-second following gap?

question.prompt: On a high-speed road in wet weather, how should you change the normal two-second following gap?
options: Keep it at two seconds
At least double it
Reduce it to one second
Increase it only at night
question.explanation: The Highway Code advises that the gap should be at least doubled on wet roads. Wet conditions also increase stopping distances.

entries.title: What does a red circular road sign generally indicate?

metadata.reference: Know Your Traffic Signs, regulatory signs

question.prompt: What does a red circular road sign generally indicate?
options: An order or restriction
A tourist attraction
A warning of a hazard only
A motorway service area
question.explanation: Circular signs generally give orders. Red circles are commonly used for prohibitions and restrictions.
question.reference: Know Your Traffic Signs, regulatory signs

questionImage.visualDescription: Red circular sign with a horizontal white bar

entries.title: You reach a STOP sign and a solid white line at a junction. What must you do?

question.prompt: You reach a STOP sign and a solid white line at a junction. What must you do?
options: Stop behind the line and wait for a safe gap
Slow down and continue if the road seems clear
Stop only if another driver sounds a horn
Stop after the line so you can see better
question.explanation: You must stop behind the solid white line at a STOP sign, then wait until there is a safe gap before moving off.

entries.title: You are turning into a side road. A pedestrian is waiting to cross that road. What should you do?

question.prompt: You are turning into a side road. A pedestrian is waiting to cross that road. What should you do?
options: Turn quickly before the pedestrian steps out
Give way to the pedestrian waiting to cross
Sound your horn to signal your intention
Wave them to wait and continue
question.explanation: When turning at a junction, you should give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road into which you are turning.

entries.title: At a normal roundabout with no signs telling you otherwise, which traffic generally has priority?

question.prompt: At a normal roundabout with no signs telling you otherwise, which traffic generally has priority?
options: Traffic approaching from your left
Traffic approaching from your right
Vehicles entering fastest
Only buses and taxis
question.explanation: Give priority to traffic approaching from your right unless road signs, signals or markings direct otherwise.

entries.title: You intend to take the first exit left at a roundabout, and signs do not say otherwise. What is the usual approach?

question.prompt: You intend to take the first exit left at a roundabout, and signs do not say otherwise. What is the usual approach?
options: Signal right and use the right lane
Enter without indicating
Signal left and approach in the left-hand lane
Use either lane but never indicate
question.explanation: For the first exit left, normally signal left and approach in the left-hand lane; continue signalling left to leave.

entries.title: You are approaching a blind bend. What is the safest choice about overtaking?

question.prompt: You are approaching a blind bend. What is the safest choice about overtaking?
options: Overtake if the vehicle ahead is slow
Overtake only while sounding your horn
Wait until you can see far enough ahead and it is safe
Drive closer to the vehicle ahead and then overtake
question.explanation: Do not overtake if you cannot see far enough ahead to be sure it is safe, such as near a bend or the brow of a hill.

entries.title: Another driver is overtaking your car. How should you normally respond?

question.prompt: Another driver is overtaking your car. How should you normally respond?
options: Accelerate so they cannot get past
Maintain a steady course and speed, slowing if necessary
Move closer to the centre line
Flash your headlights continually
question.explanation: Do not obstruct a driver who is overtaking you. Maintain a steady course and speed, and slow down if needed to let them pass safely.

entries.title: What is prohibited on the zig-zag lines approaching a pedestrian crossing?

question.prompt: What is prohibited on the zig-zag lines approaching a pedestrian crossing?
options: Parking and overtaking the vehicle nearest the crossing
Driving under 20 mph
Checking your mirrors before stopping
Giving way to pedestrians
question.explanation: You must not park on the crossing or its zig-zag lines, or overtake the moving vehicle nearest the crossing or one stopped for pedestrians.

entries.title: You are passing a stopped bus in a busy shopping street. What should you anticipate?

question.prompt: You are passing a stopped bus in a busy shopping street. What should you anticipate?
options: Pedestrians may step out unexpectedly
The road must be clear because the bus has stopped
The bus will always signal before a pedestrian crosses
Pedestrians cannot cross near a bus stop
question.explanation: Drive slowly and carefully near bus and tram stops: pedestrians may appear suddenly from behind or in front of the vehicle.

entries.title: You are driving across a pavement and cycle lane to enter a private driveway. Who should you give way to?

question.prompt: You are driving across a pavement and cycle lane to enter a private driveway. Who should you give way to?
options: Only cars on the road
Pedestrians and cyclists using the pavement and cycle lane
Only vehicles behind you
Nobody because you are entering private land
question.explanation: When crossing a pavement, cycle lane or cycle track to reach a driveway, give way to pedestrians and cyclists using those facilities.

entries.title: Fog has reduced visibility to less than about 100 metres. Which lighting rule applies?

question.prompt: Fog has reduced visibility to less than about 100 metres. Which lighting rule applies?
options: Use your headlights
Switch off all lights to reduce reflection
Use hazard warning lights continuously while moving
Only use your sidelights
question.explanation: You must use headlights when visibility is seriously reduced, generally when you cannot see farther than 100 metres.

entries.title: In heavy rain your steering suddenly feels unresponsive. What should you do first?

question.prompt: In heavy rain your steering suddenly feels unresponsive. What should you do first?
options: Brake sharply and turn hard
Ease off the accelerator and slow gradually
Accelerate to regain steering
Switch off the engine immediately
question.explanation: Water can prevent tyres gripping the road. The Highway Code advises easing off the accelerator and slowing down gradually.

entries.title: In icy conditions, stopping distances may be how much greater than on dry roads?

question.prompt: In icy conditions, stopping distances may be how much greater than on dry roads?
options: The same as in dry weather
Up to twice as great
Up to ten times as great
Always exactly three times as great
question.explanation: Stopping distances on icy or snowy roads can be ten times greater than in dry conditions. Increase separation and avoid harsh controls.

entries.title: What do double yellow lines generally mean?

question.prompt: What do double yellow lines generally mean?
options: No waiting at any time, subject to applicable exemptions
No waiting only during the evening
Parking is always allowed for up to one hour
Only commercial vehicles may wait
question.explanation: Double yellow lines indicate a prohibition of waiting at any time even without an upright sign, subject to legal exemptions.

entries.title: Except in an authorised parking space, how close to a junction does the Highway Code advise you not to stop or park?

question.prompt: Except in an authorised parking space, how close to a junction does the Highway Code advise you not to stop or park?
options: Within 2 metres
Within 5 metres
Within 10 metres
Within 25 metres
question.explanation: Rule 243 advises drivers not to stop or park opposite or within 10 metres of a junction, except in an authorised parking space.

entries.title: At night, when may you park on a road facing against the traffic flow?

question.prompt: At night, when may you park on a road facing against the traffic flow?
options: Whenever the road is quiet
Only when using a recognised parking space
Only if the headlights are on full beam
Whenever you leave the engine running
question.explanation: You must not park on a road at night facing against the flow of traffic unless you are in a recognised parking space.

entries.title: Where could strong crosswinds cause particularly sudden gusts?

question.prompt: Where could strong crosswinds cause particularly sudden gusts?
options: Only in town-centre tunnels
Open roads, bridges and gaps in hedges
Only in underground car parks
Only when driving behind a bicycle
question.explanation: Strong gusts can blow cars and other road users off course, especially on exposed roads and near gaps in hedges or bridges.

entries.title: You plan to turn just after a side street. When should you indicate?

question.prompt: You plan to turn just after a side street. When should you indicate?
options: Well before the side street regardless of confusion
Only while making the turn
After passing the side street, when your signal cannot mislead anyone
Only after you have stopped
question.explanation: Signalling too early could suggest you intend to enter the side street; time the signal so your intention is clear.

entries.title: A car ahead is signalling left but continuing straight. How should you respond?

question.prompt: A car ahead is signalling left but continuing straight. How should you respond?
options: Pull out because the indicator gives you priority
Sound your horn and pass on the left
Assume the driver has deliberately cancelled a turn
Do not assume it will turn; wait until its actual movement makes the situation safe
question.explanation: Indicators can remain on by mistake. Look for the vehicle's position and movement rather than trusting a signal alone.

entries.title: Temporary traffic lights are operating at road works. What should you do?

question.prompt: Temporary traffic lights are operating at road works. What should you do?
options: Ignore them if workers are not visible
Follow them in the same way as other traffic lights
Only stop if a police officer is present
Give way only to vehicles larger than yours
question.explanation: Temporary traffic controls are binding; a quiet work site does not remove the requirement to obey them.

entries.title: A driver flashes their headlights while approaching. What should you infer from the flash?

question.prompt: A driver flashes their headlights while approaching. What should you infer from the flash?
options: They may be drawing attention to their presence, not granting you permission to move
They are definitely giving you priority
You must speed up to pass them
They are instructing you to stop immediately
question.explanation: Flashing headlights should be used to make others aware of a vehicle, not as a guaranteed invitation to proceed.

entries.title: At a busy junction, an approaching vehicle flashes its headlights. What is the safest response?

question.prompt: At a busy junction, an approaching vehicle flashes its headlights. What is the safest response?
options: Enter immediately because the flash means it is safe
Judge the gap and priority yourself before moving
Stop indefinitely until the other driver waves
Follow the vehicle in front without looking
question.explanation: A headlight flash is ambiguous. The driver pulling out remains responsible for checking the road is clear.

entries.title: You are stationary in a built-up road at midnight and another driver is slow to move. When may you use your horn?

question.prompt: You are stationary in a built-up road at midnight and another driver is slow to move. When may you use your horn?
options: Only if a road user creates a danger that warrants a warning
To tell the driver the traffic lights have changed
Whenever you feel delayed
Continuously to attract their attention
question.explanation: The horn is for warning of presence or danger, not expressing irritation; restrictions apply when stationary and at night in built-up areas.

entries.title: You are driving at night along an unlit rural road. Which lighting is normally required?

question.prompt: You are driving at night along an unlit rural road. Which lighting is normally required?
options: Headlights, adjusted so that other road users are not dazzled
Parking lights only
Rear fog lights instead of headlights
Hazard lights continuously
question.explanation: Roads without street lighting require proper headlight use at night while avoiding dazzling oncoming traffic.

reviewImage.label: Check and use the vehicle lights correctly
reviewImage.visualDescription: Illustration of a vehicle headlamp

entries.title: A dense fog lifts and you can see clearly again. What should you do with the rear fog lights?

question.prompt: A dense fog lifts and you can see clearly again. What should you do with the rear fog lights?
options: Keep them on until the engine is switched off
Use them instead of brake lights
Switch them off so they do not dazzle drivers behind
Switch off your dipped headlights instead
question.explanation: Fog lamps can dazzle and obscure brake lamps once visibility improves, so they should not remain on without need.

entries.title: When may you use hazard warning lights while driving on a motorway?

question.prompt: When may you use hazard warning lights while driving on a motorway?
options: Whenever you exceed the speed limit
As a substitute for indicating lane changes
To ask the driver ahead to speed up
Briefly to warn traffic behind about a hazard or obstruction ahead
question.explanation: The Highway Code allows this limited moving-vehicle use on motorways or unrestricted dual carriageways to alert following drivers.

entries.title: You see a red light ahead with enough distance to brake normally. How should you slow down?

question.prompt: You see a red light ahead with enough distance to brake normally. How should you slow down?
options: Wait and brake hard at the last moment
Pull the handbrake while moving
Brake gently early, increase pressure as needed, then ease off just before stopping
Switch off the engine to slow down
question.explanation: Progressive braking helps maintain control and avoids an unnecessarily jerky stop.

entries.title: You face an unexpected emergency and must stop quickly. What should you do first?

question.prompt: You face an unexpected emergency and must stop quickly. What should you do first?
options: Turn the ignition off before braking
Use the parking brake as your first response
Accelerate to pass the danger
Apply the brakes immediately while trying to retain steering control
question.explanation: Emergency braking should begin promptly; harsh braking that locks the wheels can remove directional control.

entries.title: Your car's rear begins to slide to the left on a bend. Which steering response helps correct the skid?

question.prompt: Your car's rear begins to slide to the left on a bend. Which steering response helps correct the skid?
options: Steer sharply to the right regardless of conditions
Accelerate hard with the wheels straight
Apply full handbrake immediately
Steer towards the left while easing off the action that caused the skid
question.explanation: The Highway Code advises steering in the direction of a rear-wheel skid while removing excessive braking or acceleration.

entries.title: A road has a 60 mph limit, but a narrow bend is partly hidden by trees. What speed should you choose?

question.prompt: A road has a 60 mph limit, but a narrow bend is partly hidden by trees. What speed should you choose?
options: Exactly 60 mph because that is the posted limit
A lower speed that lets you negotiate the hazard and stop within your visible distance
The speed of the fastest car around you
60 mph unless it is raining
question.explanation: A legal speed limit is a maximum, not a target; road layout and visibility govern the safe speed.

entries.title: You are following a car at motorway speeds on a dry road. Which minimum time gap is recommended?

question.prompt: You are following a car at motorway speeds on a dry road. Which minimum time gap is recommended?
options: Half a second if you have good brakes
Exactly one second at all speeds
At least two seconds, increased when conditions require
No gap if traffic is flowing smoothly
question.explanation: At least a two-second following interval gives time to perceive and react to a vehicle slowing ahead.

reviewImage.label: Leave at least two seconds in dry conditions
reviewImage.visualDescription: Two cars separated by a following gap

entries.title: A broken centre line becomes longer with shorter gaps as you drive ahead. What does this suggest?

question.prompt: A broken centre line becomes longer with shorter gaps as you drive ahead. What does this suggest?
options: The road is becoming a motorway
You must speed up immediately
The road has no passing restrictions anywhere
A hazard may lie ahead, so take extra care before crossing the line
question.explanation: Longer white dashes and shorter gaps indicate a hazard-warning centre-line pattern.

entries.title: On a motorway, what do amber reflective road studs mark?

question.prompt: On a motorway, what do amber reflective road studs mark?
options: The left-hand edge of the carriageway
The edge beside the central reservation
The edge of a slip road
A temporary bus lane
question.explanation: Amber studs are positioned on the central-reservation side; red studs typically mark the left edge.

entries.title: A learner car driver wants to practise on a motorway. Which arrangement is permitted?

question.prompt: A learner car driver wants to practise on a motorway. Which arrangement is permitted?
options: Drive alone once the theory test has been passed
Travel with any licensed family member in an ordinary car
Travel with a friend who has held a licence for two years
Travel with a DVSA-approved driving instructor in a dual-control car displaying L plates, or D plates in Wales
question.explanation: Provisional car drivers may enter motorways only with an approved instructor in a suitably equipped, correctly plated car.

entries.title: Why should you check your mirrors and scan further ahead than usual on a motorway?

question.prompt: Why should you check your mirrors and scan further ahead than usual on a motorway?
options: Mirror checks are only needed when leaving the motorway
Cars are less likely to change lanes at high speeds
Vehicles usually travel faster, leaving less time to notice and react to changes
You have priority regardless of other drivers
question.explanation: Higher approach speeds shorten the time available to respond, making early observation essential.

entries.title: An overhead motorway message warns of debris ahead that you cannot yet see. What is the sensible response?

question.prompt: An overhead motorway message warns of debris ahead that you cannot yet see. What is the sensible response?
options: Assume the message is out of date until you see debris
Treat the warning seriously and prepare to adjust your speed and lane as directed
Drive faster to pass the affected stretch
Stop on the hard shoulder to inspect the message
question.explanation: Motorway warnings can describe hazards beyond your present view; prepare before reaching them.

entries.title: Amber motorway lights are flashing above your route. What should you do?

question.prompt: Amber motorway lights are flashing above your route. What should you do?
options: Move into the hard shoulder at once
Ignore them if you can still see the road
Treat them as permission to exceed the limit
Ease off and prepare for a hazard, following later signs before returning to normal speed
question.explanation: Flashing amber warnings signal possible danger ahead; respond by reducing speed and assessing the situation.

entries.title: A red X is displayed above the lane you are driving in. What must you do?

question.prompt: A red X is displayed above the lane you are driving in. What must you do?
options: Move safely into an open lane and do not continue along the closed one
Carry on if no workers are visible
Use that lane only when overtaking
Stop beneath the sign and wait for it to change
question.explanation: A red X identifies a lane closure and driving through that lane is prohibited.

entries.title: A red X closes the left lane at a motorway exit. What does that indicate about the exit?

question.prompt: A red X closes the left lane at a motorway exit. What does that indicate about the exit?
options: The exit cannot be used while that closure applies
The exit is reserved for cars only
You may use the shoulder to reach the exit
All vehicles must leave by that exit
question.explanation: A left-lane closure at the exit slip road means traffic must not use that exit while it remains closed.

entries.title: As you join a motorway from a slip road, who should you give priority to?

question.prompt: As you join a motorway from a slip road, who should you give priority to?
options: Drivers still behind you on the slip road
Only cars travelling faster than the speed limit
No one, because slip-road traffic has priority
Vehicles already travelling on the motorway
question.explanation: Joining drivers must judge a safe gap, adjust speed and avoid forcing established motorway traffic to brake.

reviewImage.label: Joining traffic gives way
reviewImage.visualDescription: Slip road joining a motorway carriageway

entries.title: The slip road you used continues as a new lane on the motorway. What should you normally do?

question.prompt: The slip road you used continues as a new lane on the motorway. What should you normally do?
options: Cut across all lanes as quickly as possible
Stop at the end of the merge markings
Stay in the continuing lane while settling into the traffic flow
Drive on the hard shoulder until you find a gap
question.explanation: If the slip road becomes an added motorway lane, remain in it rather than cutting unnecessarily into another lane.

entries.title: An electronic motorway sign displays a 50 mph limit within a red circle. What does it mean?

question.prompt: An electronic motorway sign displays a 50 mph limit within a red circle. What does it mean?
options: It is advice only if the normal limit is 70 mph
It applies only to goods vehicles
You must not exceed 50 mph while that signed limit applies
You may ignore it outside rush hour
question.explanation: Red-circled electronic speed limits are enforceable and override a higher usual maximum while active.

entries.title: You feel sleepy during a long motorway journey. What is the best plan?

question.prompt: You feel sleepy during a long motorway journey. What is the best plan?
options: Open a window and keep driving for another hour
Drive faster so the journey ends sooner
Leave at a safe opportunity and take a proper break at a service area
Stop directly on the carriageway to sleep
question.explanation: Monotonous high-speed driving can worsen fatigue; motorway services provide places for safe rest.

entries.title: You accidentally pass the motorway junction you needed. What should you do?

question.prompt: You accidentally pass the motorway junction you needed. What should you do?
options: Continue to the next available exit and re-plan your route
Reverse carefully along the hard shoulder
Turn across the central reservation
Stop in the live lane and ask for directions
question.explanation: Reversing and crossing the central reservation are prohibited; use the next exit rather than an unsafe manoeuvre.

entries.title: Traffic is light and you are not overtaking. Which motorway lane should you normally use?

question.prompt: Traffic is light and you are not overtaking. Which motorway lane should you normally use?
options: The left lane, moving right only when necessary and safe
The centre lane to leave space for joining traffic
Whichever lane has the best road surface
The right lane to maintain a steady speed
question.explanation: The default position is the left-hand lane, with other lanes mainly used to overtake.

entries.title: You tow a caravan on a motorway with three lanes. Can you normally use the far-right lane?

question.prompt: You tow a caravan on a motorway with three lanes. Can you normally use the far-right lane?
options: Yes, if the trailer is small
Yes, if you signal first
No, vehicles drawing a trailer are generally prohibited from that lane
Only when the traffic in all lanes is stationary
question.explanation: The Highway Code prohibits trailers in the far-right lane of motorways with three or more lanes, apart from prescribed exceptions.

entries.title: Before changing lanes to overtake on a motorway, what extra check helps detect a hidden vehicle?

question.prompt: Before changing lanes to overtake on a motorway, what extra check helps detect a hidden vehicle?
options: A brief sideways glance towards the blind spot after checking mirrors
Only looking at the interior mirror
Counting to three without looking
Flashing your headlights continuously
question.explanation: Mirrors do not show every area around the vehicle; a blind-spot check helps confirm the lane is clear.

entries.title: In heavy motorway congestion, the left lane moves slightly faster than the right. What should you do?

question.prompt: In heavy motorway congestion, the left lane moves slightly faster than the right. What should you do?
options: Keep switching lanes whenever one moves quicker
Use the hard shoulder to get ahead
Brake sharply so nobody can pass you on the left
Stay in your lane with the traffic, without weaving between lanes to gain places
question.explanation: Queuing traffic may pass traffic to its right as lanes advance differently, but deliberate weaving to overtake is discouraged.

entries.title: Your motorway exit is coming up. Which approach is recommended?

question.prompt: Your motorway exit is coming up. Which approach is recommended?
options: Brake sharply in the right-hand lane then cross to the exit
Stop on the carriageway until a gap appears
Move into the left lane in good time, signal left and slow on the slip road as needed
Leave your indicator off until after entering the slip road
question.explanation: Early lane planning and signalling allow a safe, predictable exit without late manoeuvres.

entries.title: Before driving a borrowed car, you notice a brake warning and a damaged rear lamp. What is the sensible action?

question.prompt: Before driving a borrowed car, you notice a brake warning and a damaged rear lamp. What is the sensible action?
options: Drive only on streets with low limits
Do not drive until the car is confirmed roadworthy
Switch on the hazard warning lights and continue
Trust the next MOT to identify the faults
question.explanation: The driver must use a vehicle that meets roadworthiness and lighting requirements; warning signs and defective lights need attention.

reviewImage.label: Working brake lights
reviewImage.visualDescription: Rear of a car with brake lamps illuminated

entries.title: A medical condition may make you unable to control your vehicle safely. What should you do?

question.prompt: A medical condition may make you unable to control your vehicle safely. What should you do?
options: Keep driving until the licence expires
Tell only your passengers
Inform the DVLA as required and seek medical advice about driving
Avoid reporting the condition if you drive short distances
question.explanation: Drivers must notify the licensing authority of health conditions likely to affect their driving.

entries.title: You are planning an eight-hour drive. What break pattern does the Highway Code recommend?

question.prompt: You are planning an eight-hour drive. What break pattern does the Highway Code recommend?
options: At least a 15-minute break after every two hours of driving
No breaks unless you need fuel
One break of five minutes at the end
A rest only after six hours
question.explanation: Fatigue impairs reactions; plan regular breaks of at least fifteen minutes at roughly two-hour intervals.

entries.title: You need glasses to read a modern number plate clearly from 20 metres. What must you do while driving?

question.prompt: You need glasses to read a modern number plate clearly from 20 metres. What must you do while driving?
options: Use them only when parking
Drive closer to the vehicle ahead to read its plate
Wear the required glasses or contact lenses at all times
Carry them in the glovebox without wearing them
question.explanation: Drivers must meet the number-plate eyesight standard and wear corrective lenses whenever those lenses are needed to meet it.

entries.title: You drive on a dark country lane wearing heavily tinted glasses. What is the problem?

question.prompt: You drive on a dark country lane wearing heavily tinted glasses. What is the problem?
options: Tinted lenses automatically improve night vision
They only affect your ability to read the speedometer
Tinted glasses remove headlight glare without any drawback
They may reduce your ability to see hazards in already poor visibility
question.explanation: Avoid tinted lenses at night or in poor visibility when they make it harder to see the road.

entries.title: You drank alcohol late in the evening and plan to drive early next morning. What should concern you?

question.prompt: You drank alcohol late in the evening and plan to drive early next morning. What should concern you?
options: Alcohol may still impair your driving the following morning
Sleep always removes all alcohol from the body
Coffee instantly restores safe reactions
You may drive if you feel confident
question.explanation: Alcohol takes time to leave the body, and judgement or reaction time can remain impaired well after drinking.

entries.title: A prescribed medicine makes you drowsy. What is the safest approach to driving?

question.prompt: A prescribed medicine makes you drowsy. What is the safest approach to driving?
options: Check medical advice and do not drive while your ability is impaired
Drive normally because the medicine is legal
Take extra medicine to stay alert
Only avoid motorways and continue on other roads
question.explanation: Legal medicines can still affect safe driving. Follow doctor or pharmacist advice and do not drive when impaired.

entries.title: You are setting off in a car you have never driven. What should you do before leaving?

question.prompt: You are setting off in a car you have never driven. What should you do before leaving?
options: Adjust the navigation screen while joining traffic
Leave the head restraint low to improve visibility
Depend on the first junction to learn the controls
Locate the controls and adjust the seat and mirrors
question.explanation: Knowing the controls and adjusting driving position and mirrors before moving improves control and awareness.

entries.title: A trailer blocks the rear view from your towing vehicle. What equipment might be required?

question.prompt: A trailer blocks the rear view from your towing vehicle. What equipment might be required?
options: Additional towing mirrors giving an adequate view behind
Extra front fog lamps
A second horn fitted to the trailer
Only a reflective sticker on the boot
question.explanation: When a load or trailer obstructs rearward visibility, suitable towing mirrors are required.

entries.title: A caravan sways because heavy luggage has been placed at the back. What should you do before towing?

question.prompt: A caravan sways because heavy luggage has been placed at the back. What should you do before towing?
options: Redistribute and secure the load according to the maker's guidance
Accelerate sharply so the caravan straightens
Remove the safety coupling
Increase the weight above the permitted trailer limit
question.explanation: Poor load distribution can produce dangerous snaking; heavy items should be placed appropriately over the axles with safe nose weight.

entries.title: Where is it dangerous to fit a rear-facing child seat?

question.prompt: Where is it dangerous to fit a rear-facing child seat?
options: On a rear seat with a suitable restraint
In a vehicle fitted with rear windows
In front of an active frontal airbag
In a car with a passenger-side mirror
question.explanation: An active frontal airbag can strike a rear-facing child seat in a collision, causing severe injury.

entries.title: A child needs to leave your parked car beside a busy road. Which door is usually safer to use?

question.prompt: A child needs to leave your parked car beside a busy road. Which door is usually safer to use?
options: The door beside moving traffic
Whichever door is opened fastest
The driver door even if it faces traffic
A door on the kerb side, with adult supervision
question.explanation: Using the kerb-side door usually reduces exposure to passing vehicles and cyclists.

The lorry's driver is looking straight ahead
Your car is capable of exceeding the speed limit
The road is dry even if oncoming traffic is near
question.explanation: A safe overtake needs clear road ahead and a suitable space to move back without forcing another road user to brake.

entries.title: You are about to overtake on a normal two-way road. What observation is important before moving out?

question.prompt: You are about to overtake on a normal two-way road. What observation is important before moving out?
options: Look only at the rear of the vehicle ahead
Assume nobody will approach from behind
Keep your indicator on without checking the road
Check mirrors and the blind spot for someone overtaking you
question.explanation: Another road user may already be passing you; mirrors and blind-spot checks help avoid moving into their path.

entries.title: You are overtaking a cyclist at up to 30 mph. What minimum lateral clearance is given as a guide?

question.prompt: You are overtaking a cyclist at up to 30 mph. What minimum lateral clearance is given as a guide?
options: At least 1.5 metres, with more space at higher speeds
About 20 centimetres if you sound the horn
Exactly half a metre at any speed
No gap if the cyclist is close to the kerb
question.explanation: The Highway Code advises at least 1.5 metres when passing cyclists up to 30 mph and additional room at greater speed.

entries.title: You need to pass a horse rider on a narrow road. What passing approach is advised?

question.prompt: You need to pass a horse rider on a narrow road. What passing approach is advised?
options: Stay at the speed limit and give half a metre
Travel below 10 mph and allow at least 2 metres of room
Sound the horn so the horse moves aside
Overtake very close and accelerate out
question.explanation: Horses may react unpredictably; use very low speed and generous clearance, and wait if there is not enough space.

entries.title: There is a pedestrian walking in the road without a footway. What clearance should you generally leave when passing?

question.prompt: There is a pedestrian walking in the road without a footway. What clearance should you generally leave when passing?
options: A mirror's width so other cars can pass
At least 2 metres and a low speed where possible
No extra room if the pedestrian faces traffic
Only a one-second time gap
question.explanation: Pedestrians on the carriageway need additional protection; allow space and slow to minimise danger.

entries.title: An oncoming car is approaching while you must pass parked vehicles on your side. What should you do?

question.prompt: An oncoming car is approaching while you must pass parked vehicles on your side. What should you do?
options: Force the oncoming vehicle to use the pavement
Overtake without reducing speed
Stop beside the parked cars blocking both directions
Give way to the oncoming vehicle before passing the obstruction
question.explanation: When obstructions are on your side, yielding to approaching traffic usually avoids a conflict in the narrow remaining space.

entries.title: Why is it unwise to follow closely behind a tall lorry before overtaking?

question.prompt: Why is it unwise to follow closely behind a tall lorry before overtaking?
options: It hides the road ahead and may put you outside the lorry driver's view
It increases your visibility of oncoming traffic
It makes the manoeuvre much shorter
It guarantees no other vehicle is ahead of the lorry
question.explanation: Dropping back improves sight lines and lets the larger vehicle's driver notice you in their mirrors.

entries.title: A car ahead starts overtaking a long articulated vehicle. Should you immediately follow it?

question.prompt: A car ahead starts overtaking a long articulated vehicle. Should you immediately follow it?
options: Yes; one gap is always enough for two vehicles
No; assess whether there is room and time for your own safe overtake
Yes; the first car guarantees the road ahead is clear
Only if you flash your headlights repeatedly
question.explanation: The first driver may need all the available gap, so a second driver must make an independent safety decision.

entries.title: A vehicle in front has stopped at a pedestrian crossing. What must you avoid?

question.prompt: A vehicle in front has stopped at a pedestrian crossing. What must you avoid?
options: Stopping behind it at a safe distance
Checking for people already crossing
Overtaking it while it is the nearest vehicle to the crossing
Waiting until the crossing is clear
question.explanation: Passing the closest stopped vehicle at a crossing is prohibited and may conceal pedestrians.

entries.title: You see a 'No Overtaking' sign. What does it require?

question.prompt: You see a 'No Overtaking' sign. What does it require?
options: Do not overtake until a sign or restriction ends that prohibition
Overtake only vehicles going below 20 mph
Overtake on the left if the road is quiet
Ignore it when your lane is wide
question.explanation: Regulatory no-overtaking signs restrict overtaking until the restriction is cancelled.

entries.title: You are climbing towards the brow of a hill and cannot see beyond it. What should you do about overtaking?

question.prompt: You are climbing towards the brow of a hill and cannot see beyond it. What should you do about overtaking?
options: Stay behind because oncoming traffic may be hidden
Pull out before reaching the top
Accelerate so the manoeuvre is over quickly
Use the horn and rely on the response
question.explanation: A hill crest hides the road ahead, so the required sight distance for a safe overtake is missing.

entries.title: A road is narrowing ahead and the car in front is slowing. Is this a good place to overtake?

question.prompt: A road is narrowing ahead and the car in front is slowing. Is this a good place to overtake?
options: Yes; narrowing always creates a faster lane
Yes; the slower car must move onto the verge
Only if you keep your hazard lights flashing
No; hold back because the narrowing could bring road users into conflict
question.explanation: Passing where road width reduces can force others to change speed or direction unsafely.

entries.title: You intend to turn left at a junction while following a cyclist going straight ahead. What should you do?

question.prompt: You intend to turn left at a junction while following a cyclist going straight ahead. What should you do?
options: Stay behind rather than overtake and turn across the cyclist
Pass first and turn sharply in front
Enter the cycle lane and stop across it
Use the horn to make the cyclist wait
question.explanation: Cutting left immediately after passing a cyclist creates a serious collision risk; allow them to continue.

entries.title: A driver overtakes and then moves into the space ahead of you. What should you restore?

question.prompt: A driver overtakes and then moves into the space ahead of you. What should you restore?
options: Your original speed regardless of the new gap
A position beside their rear wheel
A safe following distance behind the overtaking vehicle
A smaller gap so nobody else can enter
question.explanation: Dropping back helps restore reaction time after another vehicle moves into your stopping space.

entries.title: You are driving a slow farm vehicle and a long queue forms behind you. What should you consider?

question.prompt: You are driving a slow farm vehicle and a long queue forms behind you. What should you consider?
options: Pulling into a safe place to let faster traffic pass
Driving on the wrong side to let cars through
Accelerating beyond the vehicle's safe speed
Ignoring mirrors for the rest of the journey
question.explanation: Slow vehicles should check mirrors and use safe opportunities to allow following queues to pass.

entries.title: A driver is parked on zig-zag approach markings at a crossing. Why is this prohibited?

question.prompt: A driver is parked on zig-zag approach markings at a crossing. Why is this prohibited?
options: Zig-zags are reserved parking bays
The parked vehicle may hide people crossing and obstruct their view
It makes the vehicle more visible to drivers
The markings are intended only for heavy vehicles
question.explanation: Crossing zig-zags protect clear sight lines, and parking in the restricted area is prohibited.

entries.title: A moving car directly ahead is nearest to a pedestrian crossing. What must you not do?

question.prompt: A moving car directly ahead is nearest to a pedestrian crossing. What must you not do?
options: Keep a safe gap behind it
Check both pavements for people
Overtake that car as it approaches the crossing
Prepare to brake if necessary
question.explanation: Overtaking the moving vehicle nearest a crossing is prohibited because people may be concealed from view.

entries.title: Traffic is moving slowly, but the crossing ahead is occupied by a queue of cars. What is the safest choice?

question.prompt: Traffic is moving slowly, but the crossing ahead is occupied by a queue of cars. What is the safest choice?
options: Stop across the markings to hold your place
Wait until you can clear the entire crossing before entering it
Use the horn to move the queue
Drive up onto the pavement
question.explanation: A blocked crossing prevents pedestrians from using it safely; do not enter unless you can get clear.

entries.title: An illegally parked van blocks your view of one end of a zebra crossing. What should you anticipate?

question.prompt: An illegally parked van blocks your view of one end of a zebra crossing. What should you anticipate?
options: The crossing is closed until the van moves
People may step into view from behind the van
Pedestrians must wait for you because you cannot see them
The speed limit is suspended
question.explanation: Obstructed crossings demand particular caution because pedestrians may be hidden by parked or queuing vehicles.

entries.title: An older person is taking longer than expected to finish crossing. What should you do?

question.prompt: An older person is taking longer than expected to finish crossing. What should you do?
options: Wait patiently without edging forward or revving the engine
Move forward gently to encourage them
Sound your horn until they clear the road
Drive around them within the crossing
question.explanation: Crossing users should have time and space; intimidating them with noise or movement creates risk.

entries.title: A pedestrian has just stepped onto a zebra crossing. What is your duty?

question.prompt: A pedestrian has just stepped onto a zebra crossing. What is your duty?
options: Continue if you were approaching first
Flash headlights and keep moving
Give way and allow them to cross safely
Stop only when a red traffic light appears
question.explanation: Once a person is on a zebra crossing, drivers must give way rather than treating it as optional courtesy.

entries.title: A pedestrian waits beside a zebra crossing but has not entered it. How should you respond?

question.prompt: A pedestrian waits beside a zebra crossing but has not entered it. How should you respond?
options: Ignore them until they step into your lane
Wave while maintaining your speed
Slow if needed and give way so they can cross
Overtake the vehicle slowing ahead
question.explanation: The Highway Code advises giving way to those waiting to cross, with extra care around approaching pedestrians.

entries.title: Why should you avoid waving a pedestrian across a zebra crossing?

question.prompt: Why should you avoid waving a pedestrian across a zebra crossing?
options: Because waving always turns your brake lights off
Because pedestrians cannot see hand signals
Because it makes the crossing officially one-way
Another vehicle may be approaching that the pedestrian has not seen
question.explanation: A wave can give false reassurance about other traffic; the pedestrian must be able to judge the full situation.

entries.title: You approach a parallel crossing with cyclists waiting alongside pedestrians. What should you do?

question.prompt: You approach a parallel crossing with cyclists waiting alongside pedestrians. What should you do?
options: Be prepared to stop and give way to the cyclists or pedestrians wishing to cross
Ignore cyclists because only pedestrians use that type of crossing
Keep the speed limit and sound the horn
Overtake a vehicle stopped at the crossing
question.explanation: Parallel crossings include a cycle route and give crossing priority to cyclists and pedestrians under the stated rules.

entries.title: A zebra crossing has a central island dividing the road into two sections. How is it treated?

question.prompt: A zebra crossing has a central island dividing the road into two sections. How is it treated?
options: As one crossing like a pelican crossing
As two separate crossings
As a place where pedestrians never have priority
As a roundabout for pedestrians
question.explanation: A central refuge divides a zebra crossing into two crossings; drivers must still watch for anyone using either half.

entries.title: At a pelican crossing, the traffic signal is flashing amber and a pedestrian is still crossing. What must you do?

question.prompt: At a pelican crossing, the traffic signal is flashing amber and a pedestrian is still crossing. What must you do?
options: Accelerate because flashing amber always gives priority to cars
Sound the horn to hurry the person
Treat the amber as a full green light
Give way until the pedestrian has crossed
question.explanation: A flashing amber at a pelican crossing allows progress only when pedestrians have cleared the crossing.

entries.title: The pelican crossing signal is flashing amber and nobody is crossing. What may you do?

question.prompt: The pelican crossing signal is flashing amber and nobody is crossing. What may you do?
options: Proceed cautiously if it is safe
Stop until the light becomes green
Drive at twice the usual limit
Enter without checking either side
question.explanation: When no pedestrian remains on a pelican crossing, flashing amber permits cautious progress.

entries.title: A pelican crossing includes a central refuge island in a single signal-controlled crossing. What must you allow for?

question.prompt: A pelican crossing includes a central refuge island in a single signal-controlled crossing. What must you allow for?
options: That the crossing becomes two independent zebra crossings
Cars using the island as a parking space
Pedestrians still crossing from the opposite half
Cyclists driving on the island against traffic
question.explanation: Unlike zebra crossings split by an island, a pelican crossing continuing straight across is treated as one crossing.

entries.title: Your light turns green, but someone is still completing a crossing. What should you do?

question.prompt: Your light turns green, but someone is still completing a crossing. What should you do?
options: Drive because green automatically cancels pedestrian priority
Sound your horn and accelerate
Wait for the person to finish crossing safely
Use the opposite lane to pass them
question.explanation: A green signal does not justify driving through people who are still using the crossing.

entries.title: You approach a toucan crossing and see cyclists waiting with pedestrians. Which statement is correct?

question.prompt: You approach a toucan crossing and see cyclists waiting with pedestrians. Which statement is correct?
options: Cyclists must dismount because only pedestrians may use it
All toucan crossings have a flashing amber phase
Drivers are never required to stop at a toucan crossing
Toucan crossings serve both cyclists and pedestrians and have no pelican-style flashing amber phase
question.explanation: Toucan signals accommodate cycles as well as pedestrians; the vehicle light sequence differs from a pelican crossing.

entries.title: Why should a car driver take particular responsibility when interacting with pedestrians or cyclists?

question.prompt: Why should a car driver take particular responsibility when interacting with pedestrians or cyclists?
options: A motor vehicle can cause greater harm, so its driver should reduce the risk to others
Pedestrians are always at fault in a collision
Cyclists are banned from most roads
Larger vehicles automatically have priority
question.explanation: Those capable of causing the greatest injury have a greater responsibility to minimise danger to more vulnerable road users.

entries.title: You pass a playground just as children are gathering near the kerb. What should you do?

question.prompt: You pass a playground just as children are gathering near the kerb. What should you do?
options: Maintain speed because children are on the pavement
Sound the horn continuously to keep them in place
Drive close to the kerb so nobody can cross
Slow down and be prepared for a child to enter the road unexpectedly
question.explanation: Children may misjudge traffic or move suddenly; a reduced speed increases reaction time.

entries.title: You are about to reverse into a side street. What should you check first?

question.prompt: You are about to reverse into a side street. What should you check first?
options: Look all around and give way to pedestrians crossing the area
Look only in the interior mirror
Expect pedestrians to move out of the road
Reverse quickly to shorten the manoeuvre
question.explanation: Pedestrians are easily hidden when reversing; observe the whole area and yield before moving.

entries.title: An older pedestrian with a walking aid is crossing slowly. What is the appropriate reaction?

question.prompt: An older pedestrian with a walking aid is crossing slowly. What is the appropriate reaction?
options: Use the horn to signal that the light will change
Edge the car forward to hurry them
Be patient and leave enough time for them to cross
Drive around them within the crossing
question.explanation: People with mobility difficulties may need more time, so drivers should avoid intimidating or rushing them.

entries.title: A pedestrian uses a white cane with a red band. What does it commonly indicate?

question.prompt: A pedestrian uses a white cane with a red band. What does it commonly indicate?
options: They are a road worker directing traffic
They may be both deaf and blind
They are carrying a temporary parking permit
They are a learner driving instructor
question.explanation: The Highway Code notes that a white cane with a red band can identify a deafblind pedestrian who may not notice signals.

entries.title: A flashing amber warning appears below a school sign. What should you prepare for?

question.prompt: A flashing amber warning appears below a school sign. What should you prepare for?
options: A road closed to all vehicles for the day
A speed limit that has automatically been removed
Children crossing ahead; drive very slowly until clear of the area
A compulsory left turn at the school gate
question.explanation: School warning lights can mean children are crossing or near the road; extra caution is needed.

entries.title: You are passing a stationary school bus displaying a school-bus sign. What is especially likely?

question.prompt: You are passing a stationary school bus displaying a school-bus sign. What is especially likely?
options: The bus is about to overtake your car
Children may suddenly move into the road when boarding or leaving
The road is now a motorway
Only adults may emerge from the bus
question.explanation: Children may cross without careful observation near a stopped school bus, so pass slowly and watch closely.

entries.title: A school crossing patrol holds a 'Stop for children' sign towards you. What must you do?

question.prompt: A school crossing patrol holds a 'Stop for children' sign towards you. What must you do?
options: Proceed when you cannot see pupils
Drive around the patrol on the wrong side
Flash your headlights instead of stopping
Stop and remain stopped as directed
question.explanation: A school crossing patrol's stop signal is legally binding, even if you think the road appears clear.

entries.title: You are waiting to turn right across slow traffic. What hidden road users should you check for?

question.prompt: You are waiting to turn right across slow traffic. What hidden road users should you check for?
options: Cyclists and motorcyclists filtering along the traffic you must cross
Only heavy lorries ahead of the queue
No one, because the queue is stopped
Pedestrians inside your own vehicle
question.explanation: Two-wheelers can move past slow or stationary traffic, including in places obscured from the driver's view.

entries.title: A cyclist ahead looks over their shoulder. What might this indicate?

question.prompt: A cyclist ahead looks over their shoulder. What might this indicate?
options: They have invited you to pass closely
They may be preparing to change course or turn
They are certain to stop immediately
They are signalling that the road is empty
question.explanation: A shoulder check is often a clue that a rider is planning a move; allow time and room rather than overtaking tightly.

entries.title: A cyclist rides in the centre of a narrow lane. What is the safest response?

question.prompt: A cyclist rides in the centre of a narrow lane. What is the safest response?
options: Sound the horn until they ride in the gutter
Force your way past within the same lane
Assume they are deliberately breaking the law
Allow them to use that position and overtake only when safe
question.explanation: Cyclists may take the lane to remain visible and avoid unsafe close passes on narrow roads.

entries.title: A group of cyclists rides two abreast on a quiet narrow road. What should you consider?

question.prompt: A group of cyclists rides two abreast on a quiet narrow road. What should you consider?
options: Two-abreast cycling always makes it safe to pass between them
They must immediately form a single line for every approaching car
You should overtake without leaving the lane
They may ride that way for safety; wait for a proper overtaking gap
question.explanation: The Highway Code recognises that riding two abreast can help cyclists see and be seen in some road situations.

entries.title: A group of sheep is blocking a rural road. What is the safest action?

question.prompt: A group of sheep is blocking a rural road. What is the safest action?
options: Rev your engine to push the animals aside
Sound your horn continually until they scatter
Stop and switch the engine off until the animals have left the road
Drive between the animals while accelerating
question.explanation: Noise and movement may frighten animals, creating danger to them and nearby road users.

entries.title: You are passing a horse being led along a country lane. How should you drive?

question.prompt: You are passing a horse being led along a country lane. How should you drive?
options: Accelerate to minimise time beside the horse
Move slowly, leave generous space and be ready to stop
Use the horn to announce yourself
Drive close because horses rarely move sideways
question.explanation: Animals can startle and move unpredictably; gentle, unhurried passing reduces the chance of a dangerous reaction.

entries.title: Snow is falling heavily and your journey is not essential. What does the Highway Code advise?

question.prompt: Snow is falling heavily and your journey is not essential. What does the Highway Code advise?
options: Drive normally because modern cars cannot skid
Use only the motorway to avoid traffic
Travel late at night to find empty roads
Avoid driving until conditions are safer
question.explanation: Avoid unnecessary journeys in snow or ice; the risk remains high even with careful driving.

entries.title: You must drive in winter weather and may become stranded. Which item would be sensible to carry?

question.prompt: You must drive in winter weather and may become stranded. Which item would be sensible to carry?
options: Only a spare number plate
A bottle of oil for the windscreen
A metal bar for forcing open traffic gates
Warm clothing, a torch and basic emergency supplies
question.explanation: An emergency winter kit can help if your vehicle breaks down or you are delayed in severe conditions.

entries.title: Your windscreen has a small clear patch but snow still covers the other windows. What must you do before moving?

question.prompt: Your windscreen has a small clear patch but snow still covers the other windows. What must you do before moving?
options: Drive slowly while the heater clears the rest
Clear the snow and ice from every window needed for visibility
Use the side mirror alone
Keep the horn sounding until the view improves
question.explanation: Drivers must be able to see properly; snow and ice must be removed from windows before driving.

entries.title: Frozen dirt and snow are covering your number plates and lights. What is required?

question.prompt: Frozen dirt and snow are covering your number plates and lights. What is required?
options: Leave the snow in place to protect the paint
Clean them so the lamps work and the plates remain legible
Use hazard lights to replace covered lamps
Remove the number plates for the journey
question.explanation: Lights and registration plates must remain clean, visible and readable in winter conditions.

entries.title: A thick layer of snow has collected on your car's roof. What should you do?

question.prompt: A thick layer of snow has collected on your car's roof. What should you do?
options: Leave it to fall off while accelerating
Drive with hazard lights until it melts
Cover it with a plastic sheet and start driving
Remove snow that could slide or blow into the path of other road users
question.explanation: Loose roof snow can fall onto windscreens or create hazards for traffic following your vehicle.

entries.title: Before leaving on a long journey during a snow warning, which check is most useful?

question.prompt: Before leaving on a long journey during a snow warning, which check is most useful?
options: Check only whether the car radio works
Assume all roads are clear if your driveway is clear
Ignore updated travel bulletins
Check the route and forecast for closures or further snowfall
question.explanation: Winter roads can change quickly; forecasts and route information can prevent avoidable danger.

entries.title: A gritted road looks dry, but the temperature is below freezing. What should you remember?

question.prompt: A gritted road looks dry, but the temperature is below freezing. What should you remember?
options: Gritting guarantees the road has full summer grip
You can brake as hard as in dry conditions
The car's tyres cannot lose traction
There may still be icy patches and you need to drive cautiously
question.explanation: Treated roads can still be slippery; road surface conditions vary over short distances.

entries.title: You want to pass a snowplough working ahead. When should you consider overtaking?

question.prompt: You want to pass a snowplough working ahead. When should you consider overtaking?
options: Only if the lane you intend to use has already been cleared and the manoeuvre is safe
Whenever you can see the plough's rear lights
When the snow is deepest in the overtaking lane
Only after flashing your headlights
question.explanation: Snowploughs can throw snow sideways; using an uncleared lane to pass may be particularly dangerous.

entries.title: A winter maintenance vehicle is spreading road salt. Why should you be careful around it?

question.prompt: A winter maintenance vehicle is spreading road salt. Why should you be careful around it?
options: Its presence means the road is automatically closed
Loose salt and changing surface conditions can create hazards
You are required to follow within one metre
You may ignore normal lane markings
question.explanation: Spreading vehicles and temporary differences in grip demand extra care, especially for two-wheelers.

entries.title: A motorway variable message sign reports ice ahead. What should you do?

question.prompt: A motorway variable message sign reports ice ahead. What should you do?
options: Take the warning seriously and allow for changing grip conditions
Maintain your previous speed until skidding begins
Switch off the headlights regardless of visibility
Assume the sign applies only to lorries
question.explanation: Electronic warnings can give advance notice of slippery sections that are not immediately visible.

entries.title: When driving a manual car on an icy surface, which gear selection is generally advised?

question.prompt: When driving a manual car on an icy surface, which gear selection is generally advised?
options: The lowest gear with maximum acceleration
A relatively high gear at low speed to reduce wheel spin
Neutral while travelling downhill
Reverse gear if the road is level
question.explanation: A high gear and gentle throttle can limit sudden torque at the driven wheels on ice.

entries.title: You are approaching an icy bend. When should you reduce your speed?

question.prompt: You are approaching an icy bend. When should you reduce your speed?
options: Before reaching the bend, preferably while travelling straight
Only once you are in the sharpest part of the bend
After the car begins to slide
By applying the handbrake while turning
question.explanation: Braking gradually before a bend reduces the chance of losing grip when steering.

entries.title: How should you operate the accelerator when starting on packed snow?

question.prompt: How should you operate the accelerator when starting on packed snow?
options: Hard enough to spin the tyres until they grip
In repeated full-throttle bursts
Smoothly and gently to avoid wheel spin
Only after turning the steering wheel fully
question.explanation: Sudden acceleration can break tyre traction; gentle inputs help maintain control.

entries.title: While travelling on ice, you notice that tyre noise has almost disappeared. What may this indicate?

question.prompt: While travelling on ice, you notice that tyre noise has almost disappeared. What may this indicate?
options: Very little tyre grip on the surface
That the tyres have become warmer and safer
That the road has turned into a gravel surface
That the car's exhaust is blocked
question.explanation: Tyres can make very little noise on ice, which may be a warning of the slippery surface.

entries.title: You are unsure whether a quiet stretch of road is icy. How could you cautiously assess the available grip?

question.prompt: You are unsure whether a quiet stretch of road is icy. How could you cautiously assess the available grip?
options: In a safe place, brake very gently and notice the response
Brake violently in a busy traffic lane
Accelerate hard and see whether the tyres spin
Steer sharply while close to the kerb
question.explanation: The Highway Code describes cautiously testing grip with gentle braking in a safe place, not provoking a skid.

entries.title: You are about to leave your car parked at the roadside. What must you do with its parking brake?

question.prompt: You are about to leave your car parked at the roadside. What must you do with its parking brake?
options: Leave it released so the car can be pushed
Use it only when parked on steep hills
Replace it by turning the headlights on
Apply it securely before leaving the vehicle
question.explanation: The Highway Code requires the parking brake to be applied before a parked vehicle is left.

entries.title: Before opening the driver's door beside a cycle lane, how can you reduce the risk of striking a cyclist?

question.prompt: Before opening the driver's door beside a cycle lane, how can you reduce the risk of striking a cyclist?
options: Open the door quickly so it is visible
Sound the horn and open without looking
Check mirrors and look over your shoulder, ideally opening with the far hand
Wait until a cyclist is directly alongside the door
question.explanation: Looking all around, including over the shoulder, helps prevent 'dooring' passing cyclists or motorcyclists.

entries.title: Passengers are getting out of a parked car beside a busy road. Which side is generally safer?

question.prompt: Passengers are getting out of a parked car beside a busy road. Which side is generally safer?
options: The kerb side, away from moving traffic
The side next to the fastest vehicles
The side with the shortest door opening
Any side because parked cars have priority
question.explanation: Using the kerb-side door reduces exposure to passing traffic, especially for children.

entries.title: You park an electric vehicle beside a public charger. What extra hazard should you consider?

question.prompt: You park an electric vehicle beside a public charger. What extra hazard should you consider?
options: The vehicle has no parking brake
The charger makes all nearby parking rules inapplicable
Pedestrians may not use the pavement at charging points
Loose charging cables could trip pedestrians
question.explanation: Keep charging cables tidy and avoid trailing them across the route used by pedestrians.

entries.title: Is it permitted to park within the marked zig-zag approach area of a pedestrian crossing?

question.prompt: Is it permitted to park within the marked zig-zag approach area of a pedestrian crossing?
options: Yes, if the engine is switched off
Yes, for a short phone call
No, the marked crossing area must be kept clear
Yes, as long as a passenger remains inside
question.explanation: Parking on a crossing or its restricted zig-zag approaches is prohibited and can obstruct visibility.

entries.title: You see a clearway sign on a stretch of road. What should you understand?

question.prompt: You see a clearway sign on a stretch of road. What should you understand?
options: Stopping on the carriageway is generally prohibited by the clearway restriction
The road is only for vehicles over 7.5 tonnes
You may park whenever traffic is light
The road is a designated loading bay
question.explanation: Clearways restrict stopping, with any exceptions indicated by the relevant signs.

entries.title: A tram lane is in operation and not available to ordinary cars. May you stop and park in it?

question.prompt: A tram lane is in operation and not available to ordinary cars. May you stop and park in it?
options: Yes, provided hazard lights are flashing
No, parking or stopping in the operating tram lane is prohibited
Only if you are collecting a parcel
Yes, when tram traffic is not visible
question.explanation: The Highway Code prohibits stopping or parking in restricted tram or cycle lanes during their period of operation.

entries.title: A parking bay is marked for Blue Badge holders only. When may you use it?

question.prompt: A parking bay is marked for Blue Badge holders only. When may you use it?
options: When you are entitled to do so under the bay's restrictions
Whenever every ordinary parking bay is occupied
If you intend to park for less than five minutes
Anytime if you leave a phone number on the dashboard
question.explanation: Reserved bays are for authorised users only; inconvenience is not a valid reason to occupy them.

entries.title: You park partly across a narrow entrance so that vehicles cannot reach an emergency access road. What is wrong?

question.prompt: You park partly across a narrow entrance so that vehicles cannot reach an emergency access road. What is wrong?
options: The car may be causing an unnecessary obstruction or danger
It is acceptable when the engine is off
Emergency access must be provided only after sunset

question.explanation: Planning avoids wasteful speed changes. Coasting reduces control and tailgating removes reaction space.
